commit 921702ad04209f55adfd19a79a1f4c91332abe6d
ordinal 47
date 2026-08-05 17:39:07 -0700
author Matt Stults
subject Quality read: the ladder cannot close the gap; index-builder review (REVISE, 4 major)
RELEVANCE_QUALITY_READ.md answers the go/no-go question directly. Tool at +0.3088
mean MCC against a +0.5555 frontier-panel bar. The six closed cycles since 2026-08-04
moved that by +0.0003 TOTAL, against the project's own noise floor of 0.0316-0.037 --
two orders of magnitude below. The only real gain in the whole record (+0.072) came
from re-selecting the behaviour-atom artifact: an instrument change, not a mechanism.

Upper bound on the remaining ladder, under an ORACLE assumption of perfect landing
and zero collateral: 42% of the gap. Honest central estimate: 15-28%. And the oracle
assumptions are already refuted -- S5 measures zero flips, S6's own Tier-1 rules 14-15
of its 26 targets out of bounds while being 65% of the bound's gain, S3b reaches
79/155, and the 60-case threshold class has no mechanical owner BY DESIGN (consuming
those verdicts is the panel-fitting the invariants exist to prevent).

Two structural findings that outrank the arithmetic:
- 43% of the metric's error mass is not in the census at all (256 of 447 disagreement
  passages covered). Every planned cycle aims at the 57% that is.
- The census  field -- the mechanical proxy for 'cases where the panel is
  arguably wrong' -- is perfectly block-segregated by behaviour (129/0/0, 58/0/27,
  39/41/0). Zero mixing across 294 judgments is a per-run seat stance, not per-case
  judgment. It must not be quoted as a panel-quality measurement. A recalibrated
  cross-behaviour pass is the highest-value cheap follow-up on the board.

README correction, in the tool's favour: the bag-of-words control is +0.108 on the
DEV cells, not the +0.19 published (that is HANDOFF's 9-behaviour figure sitting in a
3-behaviour table). Real lift is ~2.9x, not ~1.6x.

INDEX_BUILDER_REVIEW.md: REVISE, 0 blocking, 4 major. The refactor is a genuine noop,
confirmed three independent ways including a route that does not use the author's
harness. What needs work is the guarantee apparatus: the anti-branch guard does not
catch an axis added on a NEW config key (reproduced -- 15 tests pass with a live
off-registry branch), and the reconstruction gate prints BASELINE MATCH while the
recorded threshold and predicted set are never replayed (reproduced by mutating
apply_rule to return 0.0 for every input).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

----END----

subject S5 design: mechanical fixes applied; the zero-flip question RECORDED, not decided
Per S5_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW.md. Every number re-verified from disk by the applying
agent; no review claim failed.

- ENG-B1: new 0.5.1 manifest section. S5 was not expressible as a cycle at all -- it
  changes no file, and the file it points at is closure-pinned, so the driver refuses
  at OPEN three different ways. Now specifies shape, files_to_change (the

  the cycle log rather than named statically.
- ENG-B2: the expected effect was atom-channel only while 16 of 24 changed clauses
  move through section spillover. Now two-part, with section_spillover added as a
  permitted adjudicable flip tag.
- ENG-B3: the patient-composition contract was false under pricing 1.2. Proven again
  on m0355 -- a chained clause atom IS reached by the overlay once 1.2 dechains it.
  Rewritten to state the real contract: the patient factor must apply to subsumption
  credit using the clause atom's preserved chain, or the overlay launders patient
  structure.
- ENG-B4 and staleness: PRICING_VERSION 1.2 not 1.1; six closed cycles (5 keep, 1
  revert) not three; overlay-OFF true of the frozen cuts only; cycle 5 reverted, so
  5.3's premise is counterfactual and is now conditional on S3b.
- SCI-M2: the 7-flips-for-a-2-edge-family calibration struck as refuted (measured 0 on
  the current corpus); the one-family-per-cycle rule kept on better grounds.
- SCI-B2: a conditional pre-registration written at mechanism level -- 8 subsumption
  records on named clauses, 1.6812 at kind_factor 0.4, latent manipulation at df 8 /
  idf 4.2030, 24 clauses changing of which 16 section-only.

The zero-flip finding is recorded in a fenced OPEN STRATEGIC QUESTION block naming
the three options without choosing, pointing at DECISIONS_FOR_MATT Decision 1. The
pre-built disclosure -- measuring S5 before OPEN spends its temporal guarantee, and
no procedure restores it -- is mandatory in both the prediction notes and the
decision justification.

subject DECISIONS: fill in Decision 6 with the measured answer
The strategic question now has numbers. Six cycles moved the metric +0.0003 against a
noise floor of 0.032-0.037; the remaining ladder's oracle ceiling is 42% of the gap
and its honest estimate is 15-28%, resting on assumptions already refuted. Two
structural findings outrank the arithmetic: 43% of the measured error was never
catalogued, and the field that would tell us how much of the gap is the panel's fault
is confounded with which seat run produced it.

Recommendation recorded: stop treating the frontier bar as the objective, do not

commit 2c96735271a6ea9a3f7e14d181f6ea95a8f53254
ordinal 50
date 2026-08-05 17:43:53 -0700
author Matt Stults
subject S6 shape partition computed mechanically; README control number corrected
SHAPE PARTITION. S6's central anti-fitting gate -- add vocabulary only where the
concept exists nowhere, fix the QUESTION where it already exists -- was applied by
prose in a design document and could not be applied by the seat at all (the seat is
deliberately blind to query vocabularies). shape_partition.py computes it from the
artifacts and freezes a sha-pinned output.

Result: 14 shape_b / 12 shape_a, against the design's hand-assignment. 17 of 26
clauses lack a usable correct assignment -- 13 unambiguous inversions, 2 where the
design contradicts itself (dual family membership), 3 the design never books anywhere.
The S6 review's 'already in another query' figure of 14 is confirmed exactly; its '15
of 26' is off by one (14 under any self-consistent reading).

The join key matters and was verified, not assumed: containment.dechain_name strips
the chain and PRESERVES polarity; grammar.stem_of strips polarity too. On these
artifacts the two disagree on exactly m0242 and m0253, and in both cases stem_of would
call a genuine Shape-A clause Shape-B by merging mustnot_ into shouldnot_. A sibling
design's decision material made exactly that error.

A third state was adopted from the data rather than invented: shape_a_polarity_variant
(2 cases), the only non-empty candidate of four tested, and the highest duplicate risk
in Shape A -- a seat adding an atom there is one prefix away from minting the
duplicate the design forbids.

Fenced FORBIDDEN, not QUERY_MODULES, with the reasoning in the module docstring: it
reads a panel-derived verdict file, and routing that read through an indirection to
pass the static scan would convert a disclosed reader into a laundering path.
Panel-blindness is enforced positively instead -- classify() has no argument a panel
value can arrive through.

README: the bag-of-words control row said +0.19, which is HANDOFF's 9-behaviour figure
in a 3-behaviour table. Re-measured independently twice: +0.108. The correction is in
the tool's favour (2.9x lift, not 1.6x). Added a pointer to the quality read so nobody
quotes +0.309 as a trajectory without seeing that six cycles moved it +0.0003.

test_ladder: the no-live-client test wrote into a gitignored directory, so the suite
could not pass from a clean clone. It now owns its own tmp_path. The output location
was incidental to what the test asserts.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

----END----

commit 7e701dc3b4d3e6a562fba5ebf99ca708c8ea8d43
ordinal 51
date 2026-08-05 17:49:55 -0700
author Matt Stults
subject PROJECT_ASSESSMENT: the funding memo
Written for a reader with no background. Answers the three questions asked: is this
worth continuing to fund, is there a nearby pivot, or should we just use frontier
models.

The finding it turns on: the long tail is not made of missing rules, it is made of
judgement. Four measured walls -- the formal representation loses the deciding fact
(two structurally identical passages must be answered differently); some questions the
document simply does not settle; some passages protect people they never name; and
widening coverage adds errors about as fast as it removes them. Rules can RELOCATE
that judgement into reviewable artifacts, which is genuinely valuable, but they cannot
remove it. That is why returns diminish.

Recommendation: stop funding accuracy work on the rule engine; fund the auditability
machinery (which is model-agnostic and works wrapped around a frontier model) and the
ranked-audit axis a human expert actually endorsed; run two cheap decisive experiments
first. If the only goal is quality with little human effort, frontier models are
better today and nothing in our plan closes that.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

----END----

commit 7421852a97a236a7a3bad7093aa7a783a0df76b9
ordinal 52
date 2026-08-05 17:53:58 -0700
author Matt Stults
subject Fix join_facts: the refusal facts were keyed on WHO computed the joins
Reported as 'evaluate() with caller-supplied joins + join_version=2 does not populate
join_facts'. Reproduced first: a precomputed v2 join handed to evaluate() reports
degenerate_quote_refused == 0 where it should be 1, because the refused passage gets
silently rebooked into verbatim_but_unsegmented while the accounting identity still
balances -- the 'misdescribes its own measurement' failure exactly.

Diagnosis, not a symptom patch: the facts lookup was nested inside the
'if joins is None' branch, so it was conditioned on who computed the joins rather than
on which join version was declared. join_facts is evaluate's only input to the
refusal stratum, so a caller that precomputes joins -- which is the S8 checkpoint
census's exact shape -- loses the whole refusal-reporting path even with
join_version=2 passed explicitly.

Now derived from the declared version unconditionally. The cache is keyed identically,
so the previously-working path recomputes nothing, and v1 stays None (the legacy join
has nothing to disclose). No signature, output shape, or v1 number changes.

Two adjacent gaps found and deliberately NOT widened into this diff -- both recorded
as Decision 8: cell_evaluate has no join_version parameter at all, so a checkpoint
routing through it would silently measure and report v1; and evaluate never surfaces
the restriction fact the design calls 'a fact the caller must see'.

commit d3f3403b044acfc2c5ada098167b3c9ebb348a85
ordinal 54
date 2026-08-05 18:01:18 -0700
author Matt Stults
subject PROJECT_ASSESSMENT: add Option D, the version built for the actual economics
The memo compared our cheap tool against frontier-per-query and skipped the option
that matches the real cost structure: high one-time cost per DOCUMENT, low cost per
behaviour and per iteration. Reframed by Matt, correctly.

Option D: a frontier mapping pass, run once per document, making each decision
explicitly with a written explanation and a citation, auditable and human-correctable
afterwards -- then unlimited cheap behaviour queries against it.

Our evidence favours this more than it favours the rule ladder. Every wall we hit was
representation loss, never matching failure -- the two structurally identical passages
are identical precisely BECAUSE the annotation dropped who the harm falls on. The only
real gain in the project's history (+0.072) came from improving an instrument; six
cycles of matching work gave +0.0003. Cost is order $20-60 once, and the correction
machinery is already designed.

The reframing that matters: the long tail may be much shorter in dimension-space than
in rule-space. Four walls map to four missing annotation DIMENSIONS -- who is affected,
what is implied but unsaid, the scope decision with its reasoning, and what kind of
obligation a passage is. Four found by failing four times. If the true count is 5-15,
one well-designed pass carries them all.

What is unproven is exactly one thing and it is cheap to test: does a behaviour-BLIND
annotation generalize to behaviours nobody had in mind? The six held-out behaviours
exist to answer this, and it is a far better use of a one-shot resource than confirming
the rule ladder plateaued.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

----END----

commit 775514fd0222413c7e8db0d1f6ae1d4f61d844d4
ordinal 55
date 2026-08-05 18:06:31 -0700
author Matt Stults
subject FRONTIER_LAYER_EXPERIMENT: the staged design, with the measurement made explicit
Matt's structure: burn one behaviour as pure dev to build the frontier-adjudicated
layer; generalize to the other two with fixes allowed, to LEARN; then freeze and run
the held-out behaviours to see whether it is going to be like that for every behaviour.

Two things this adds.

WHICH BEHAVIOUR TO BURN, from the census cause distribution: helpfulness. It carries
44% of catalogued failures, the most distinct classes (7 of 8), and the ~30 cases no
current mechanism touches at all -- passages about answer quality, where relevance is
not a question about parties. Designing against it forces the schema to invent the
dimension we know is missing rather than re-deriving ones we already designed.

But NO SINGLE BEHAVIOUR EXERCISES EVERYTHING: helpfulness has zero section-prior cases,
harm-avoidance has zero threshold-drift, caution lacks both rare classes. That is not a
flaw in the plan, it is the reason stage 2 exists -- but it must be pre-registered or
stage 2's fixes get misread.

THE MEASUREMENT DISCIPLINE, which is the part that decides the question: stage 2 is
worthless if fixes are made freely and uncounted -- it becomes a second dev set. So
pre-register the classes stage 1 could not have exercised, then classify every stage-2
fix as EXPECTED (a dimension for a class stage 1 never saw -- fine, the count is
finite), ALARMING (a class stage 1 DID exercise and the schema still failed here --
predicts stage 3 needs the same forever), or FATAL (a per-behaviour special case -- the
tail is unbounded, stop). The delta between stage 2's fix count and stage 3's IS the
experiment.

Also: two one-shot resources exist and answer different questions -- six held-out
behaviours (across behaviours) and the sealed second document (across documents).
Stage 3 spends the first; reserve the second entirely. Recommend splitting the six 3+3.

Cost priced honestly: $20-60 per annotation pass, 5-10 passes in stage 1, so $100-600 --
one to two orders of magnitude over the current $8.50 ceiling. Small absolutely, but it
needs an explicit budget decision, and it would be the first spend whose result changes
what we believe rather than moving a metric by less than its noise floor.

Stop conditions stated in advance so they are not rationalized later.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

----END----

commit bb4ebc302e3ba27d1e364199975f021194c57e88
ordinal 56
date 2026-08-05 18:14:44 -0700
author Matt Stults
subject Decision 8: cell_evaluate can select the join, and the restriction fact reaches callers
FIX 1 -- cell_evaluate had no join_version parameter at all. It hard-defaulted to v1
and passed nothing down, so a checkpoint caller routing through it could not select v2
and would silently measure and REPORT v1: a measurement that misdescribes its own
configuration, the exact failure the census config-identity work was done to prevent.

The non-obvious part: threading the version required widening _join_key, the cache key.
The variant set changes WHICH clauses a passage joins to, so without it the
module-global join cache would serve the uniform-variant answer to a mixed-variant run.
A version-selection fix that left the cache key alone would have looked correct and
silently returned the wrong join.

FIX 2 -- evaluate never returned join_facts, so `restricted` (the disclosed
full-corpus fallback the design calls a fact the caller must see, never silent) did not
reach the caller at all. Now surfaced as join.facts: additive, inert under v1, no
recomputation, no existing key changed meaning.

This was deferred earlier on the grounds that it changed an output shape. That was a
category, not a risk assessment. All 14 consumers of evaluate's result were enumerated:
every one reads named keys, none enumerates keys, compares dicts wholesale, or
serializes the result into a recorded artifact -- so no recorded artifact's shape
shifts. The deferral was over-cautious and the check took minutes.

BEHAVIOUR CHANGE on an error path, recorded deliberately: evaluate and clause_joins now
RAISE on an impossible option pairing (mixed_variants under v1) where they previously
accepted and ignored it. That matches MODULE_MAP §11's anti-rule -- a silently-ignored
flag makes the config header's own record false -- but it is a change, so it is named
here rather than buried.

Suite 2198 passed / 4 skipped, verified before commit (+4, exactly the new tests).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
